definitions.explanation: To hold or perform a wedding ceremony. Refers to the ceremony itself, not the reception that follows.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧{挙式|きょしき}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We're holding our wedding ceremony next month.

examples.japanese: {挙式|きょしき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日取|ひど}り→日取り：12952_hidori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧。
examples.english: We're deciding on the date for the wedding ceremony.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{神前|しんぜん}{式|しき}→神前式：28943_shinzenshiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{挙式|きょしき}した⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、⟦{披露宴|ひろうえん}→披露宴：05636_hirouen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: The couple held their wedding ceremony in a Shinto style, then held the reception afterward.

notes:
{挙式|きょしき} names the ceremony itself — the vows, the ring exchange, the religious or civil rite — as distinct from the ⟦{披露宴|ひろうえん}→披露宴：05636_hirouen⟧ (reception) that typically follows it in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挙式|きょしき}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to hold a wedding ceremony
- {挙式|きょしき}{日|び}: the date of the ceremony
- {挙式|きょしき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{形式|けいしき}→形式：00211_keishiki⟧: the style of ceremony (Shinto, Christian, civil, etc.)
- {挙式|きょしき}のみ⟦プラン→プラン：00345_puran⟧: a ceremony-only plan (no reception)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧: wedding ceremony — the everyday word for the event as a whole, including sense of the occasion; {挙式|きょしき} is the more formal, procedural term used in invitations and planning.
- {式|しき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{挙|あ}げる→挙げる：27889_ageru⟧: to hold a ceremony — a common set phrase using the same {式|しき} but with ⟦{挙|あ}げる→挙げる：27889_ageru⟧ instead of the noun-verb {挙式|きょしき}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧.
